title: Annual Safety Report Annex 4 sector tables and World Air Transport Statistics aircraft-use releases

public_sources.title: IATA Safety Report 2014
public_sources.coverage_observation: Annex 4 publishes sectors by manufacturer/model for 2010-2014.

public_sources.title: IATA Safety Report 2016
public_sources.coverage_observation: Annex 4 publishes sectors by manufacturer/model for 2012-2016.

public_sources.title: IATA Safety Report 2019
public_sources.coverage_observation: Annex 4 publishes sectors by manufacturer/model for 2015-2019 and identifies Ascend / Flightglobal Advisory Service as the sector-data source.

public_sources.title: IATA Launches 2024 World Air Transport Statistics Report
public_sources.coverage_observation: IATA reports 10 million global Boeing 737 flights in 2024, explicitly including all variants.

public_sources.title: IATA Releases 2025 World Air Transport Statistics
public_sources.coverage_observation: IATA reports 10.8 million Boeing 737 flights in 2025 and 10.5 million in its 2019 comparison, explicitly including all variants.

public_sources.title: IATA Releases 2025 Safety Report
public_sources.coverage_observation: IATA states that OAG is its main sector-data source and that historical sector figures may change when source information or accident criteria are revised.

verified_observations.historical_annex4: Public IATA Safety Report editions expose global annual sector counts by manufacturer/model for overlapping five-year windows covering at least 2010-2019.
verified_observations.boeing_granularity: The public Annex 4 tables separate Boeing 717/727/737/747/757/767/777/787, but the 737 row aggregates variants rather than separating 737 Classic, NG, 737-800 or MAX.
verified_observations.recent_wats: Public WATS releases expose recent global flight-frequency observations for Boeing 737 all variants, including 2024 and 2025.
verified_observations.revision_risk: Overlapping report vintages do not guarantee identical historical values; IATA explicitly warns that sector figures can change as source information is updated.

limitations: No continuous public 2020-2023 manufacturer/model sector table has yet been demonstrated in this audit.
Boeing 737 all-variant aggregation is not sufficient to manufacture separate 737 NG/737-800 versus MAX 8 exposure.
Historical values require a declared vintage rule because IATA/OAG sector data can be revised.
The project must not copy full copyrighted tables into the public repository; retain source metadata and derived audit observations only unless redistribution rights are clear.
scientific_gate_effect: promising G2 evidence only; baseline_present remains false until complete compatible cohort-year coverage is demonstrated
